newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NUGGETS NAME BRISTOW HEAD OF BASKETBALL OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NUGGETS NAME BRISTOW HEAD OF BASKETBALL OPERATIONS.

text.p: The Denver Nuggets named Allan Bristow their new vice president of basketball operations Wednesday, and he said he would spend the next week evaluating players, coaches and executives with an eye toward possible changes before the NBA trading deadline on February 20.

Bristow replaced Bernie Bickerstaff, who began the season as coach and president of the Nuggets but is now the coach of the Washington Bullets. Longtime NBA coach Dick Motta replaced Bickerstaff on the sidelines and also will be evaluated.

"We've got seven or eight good days of calling up general managers who I know," said Bristow, who coached the Charlotte Hornets for five seasons and served as an assistant with the Nuggets for five more.

"All of us are going to be evaluated and I can't tell you everything that is going to happen tomorrow, a week from here or whatever," Bristow said. "But Dick Motta is our coach (and) let's just keep things status quo and we'll see what happens."
It has been a turbulent season for the Nuggets, who are fifth in the Midwest Division with a 16-33 record, 4 1/2 games out of the final Western Conference playoff spot.
During the off-season, they lost centre Dikembe Mutombo to Atlanta via free agency and traded guard Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf to Sacramento for Sarunas Marciulionis, whose knees are so bad he may retire.
Another deal netted NBA assist leader Mark Jackson from Indiana, but first-round draft pick Efthimis Retzias never agreed to terms and second-round pick Jeff McInnis was suspended, then waived.

Bickerstaff was 4-9 before stepping aside for Motta, who lost 10 of his first 11 games and is 12-24 this season. Injuries have prevented the Nuggets from developing any sort of consistency this season and Bristow said the players are wary of change.
"I talked to the staff, the players and coaches, and there's a little uneasiness -- 'what's going to happen?' and 'is my job secure?' I'm going to try and iron those things out," said Bristow.

"I'm not saying I've got a 100 percent handle on all 12 or 13 players that we have, but I think I've got a handle of the players that are part of the Denver Nuggets. I would say there's a strong nucleus that we would want to keep together."

Bristow led the Hornets to a 41-41 mark last season, one game shy of the final Eastern Conference playoff berth. His best season came in 1994-95, when the Hornets won 50 games and advanced to the conference semifinals. He was 207-203 in five seasons in Charlotte.
Bristow was vice president of basketball operations for the Hornets in 1990-91 before becoming coach. He also was an assistant for the Nuggets from the 1984-85 through the 1989-90 seasons.
After consecutive playoff seasons in 1994 and 1995, the Nuggets missed the post-season last year and are in danger of doing so again this year for the fifth time in the last eight seasons.
